name: VIVA
description: Large vision language models (VLMs) have demonstrated significant potential for integration into daily life, making it crucial for them to incorporate human values when making decisions in real-world situations. This paper introduces VIVA, a benchmark for VIsion-grounded decision-making driven by human VAlues. While most large VLMs focus on physical-level skills, our work is the first to examine their multimodal capabilities in leveraging human values to make decisions under a vision-depicted situation. VIVA contains 1,240 images depicting diverse real-world situations and the manually annotated decisions grounded in them. Given an image there, the model should select the most appropriate action to address the situation and provide the relevant human values and reason underlying the decision. Extensive experiments based on VIVA show the limitation of VLMs in using human values to make multimodal decisions. Further analyses indicate the potential benefits of exploiting action consequences and predicted human values.
evaluation_method: accuracy (for action selection) + human_eval/qualitative scoring for value/reason explanations
reputation: New benchmark (2024) that has attracted attention in multimodal value-alignment research but has limited adoption so far.
notes: Small dataset (1,240 images); annotations subject to human value subjectivity; multimodal (vision+language) evaluation includes both discrete action selection and free-form explanation, making automatic evaluation partially reliant on human judgment; potential label ambiguity.
